agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Asking PSF ($1,701) sits right at URA median ($1,704) — fair, not overpaid. 6.89%/yr CAGR on 45 transactions is reliable and above the RCR ~5.8% baseline. 999-year tenure removes lease-decay risk that plagues 99yr peers. Price ($1.83M) is in the liquid sweet spot. 212 units is on the smaller side but adequate; reviews praise facilities/space. MMR 752 / on frontier corroborates. Negatives: 1.2km to Boon Keng MRT (14-min walk) caps tenant appeal somewhat.

agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Strengths: 3-min walk to NE15 Buangkok is a genuine liquidity and rental driver; 176 transactions is a deep, reliable base; 6.07%/yr CAGR is solid. But asking $1,927psf is ~4.8% over the $1,838 URA median — paying up. At 872sqft this is a very tight 3BR (shoebox-ish per bedroom), which narrows the family buyer pool that 3BRs normally rely on. 99yr from 2012 leaves ~85yrs — fine. MMR 682 / off frontier is middling. The MRT proximity rescues it from Avoid, but the PSF premium on a cramped layout caps it at Neutral.

listings.mrt_info: 3 min (280 m) from NS18 Braddell MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: Large 1,442sqft 3BR at Braddell MRT (280m), $2.4M / $1,664psf — a striking ~15% below the URA median ($1,967). Generous size, two-MRT access and a responsive MCST make this an efficient, well-priced D12 hold; the discount reflects the bay-window/balcony-heavy layout rather than a defect.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Asking $1,664psf vs $1,967 URA median is a ~15% discount — the standout value in this batch on an absolute-PSF basis, driven by the large 1,442sqft format (price-per-foot compresses on big units). 134 transactions = liquid, reliable; 5.64%/yr CAGR is healthy. 280m to Braddell NS18 plus Toa Payoh within reach is a real transit/rental anchor. Reviews note responsive MCST and good maintenance. Caveats: $2.4M sits at the upper edge of the liquid band, and reviews flag thin soundproofing and bay-window/balcony space that inflates strata area — partly why PSF reads cheap. Net: large, central, MRT-fronting, fairly-to-cheaply priced. MMR 746 / on frontier supports.

listings.mrt_info: 15 min (1.25 km) from EW23 Clementi MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: Newly-TOP'd (2023) D05 mega-development 3BR, 969sqft at $2.1M / $2,167psf. Huge 632-txn liquid base and One-North/Clementi proximity, but a compact layout and the high PSF on a recently-launched project (resale-only CAGR de-rates to 5.15%) mean limited near-term upside after developer pricing.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Liquidity is exceptional — 1,468 units and 632 URA transactions make this one of the most tradeable assets in the batch. D05 One-North/Clementi tech-hub demand underpins rentals. But: has_new_launch_bias=true, and the resale-only rate de-rates from 6.14% to 5.15%/yr — the headline appreciation is partly developer-pricing inflation. At $2,167psf on a 3-year-old project, much of the launch premium is already in the price, so 5-7yr upside is capped. 969sqft is a tight 3BR (efficient but family-pool-limiting), and 1.25km/15-min to Clementi MRT is a real walkability gap for a mega-project. Developer SingHaiyi has a mixed quality record (Pasir Ris One complaints). Solid, liquid, but fully priced — Neutral.

agent_evaluation.summary: Freehold D15 3BR (1,528sqft) at $2.0M / $1,309psf, 470m to Kembangan MRT — looks cheap, but Radix is a 21-unit boutique with only 4 URA transactions and 3.2% yield. The headline MMR 807 is an artifact of thin data; illiquidity is the real story.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: On paper attractive: freehold, large 1,528sqft, $1,309psf well under the (thin) $1,445 median, 470m to Kembangan EW6, desirable D15. But the development has just 21 units total and only 4 URA transactions — the 7.49%/yr CAGR and MMR 807 / score 807 are statistically meaningless and must be heavily discounted (anti-anchoring). A 21-unit block means shallow exit liquidity: any single forced seller moves the market, and price discovery is poor. Reviews note exclusivity/privacy as a plus but that is an own-stay virtue, not an investment one. Freehold + large size + location give real downside support, so not an Avoid — but thin liquidity and unreliable appreciation data cap it firmly at Neutral.

listings.mrt_info: 6 min (500 m) from CC8 Dakota MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: UOL-built D14 Dakota 3BR (1,281sqft) at $2.9M / $2,264psf — ~5.6% above URA median ($2,144), in the thin >$2.5M band, with documented military-jet noise from nearby Paya Lebar Airbase. Quality developer and MRT proximity, but priced rich with a real noise overhang.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Genuine positives: UOL is a top-tier developer, 500m to Dakota CC8, 144 URA txns = liquid base, central D14. But the case weakens on three fronts: (1) asking $2,264psf is ~5.6% over the $2,144 median; (2) at $2.9M it's above the liquid sweet spot, thinning exit demand; (3) reviews specifically and repeatedly flag loud military jet noise (8am-9pm weekdays/Sat) from Paya Lebar Airbase — a tenant/resale negative the data can't capture. Appreciation is the weakest in the batch at 5.28%/yr. MMR 559 is only modestly above market-typical. The Paya Lebar airbase relocation (post-2030) is a long-dated catalyst that could eventually remove the noise, but that's beyond the 5-7yr horizon. Net: fully-priced with a noise discount needed — Neutral leaning cautious.

listings.mrt_info: 12 min (990 m) from CR9 Serangoon North MRT Station

agent_evaluation.summary: 999-year D19 3BR (1,076sqft) at $1.58M / $1,468psf — the top algo score (MMR 827) but on a 17-unit micro-development with only 6 URA transactions, a 2.6% yield, and an unknown single-project developer. The headline 13.2%/yr CAGR is statistical noise; this is an illiquid boutique, not an investment-grade asset.
agent_evaluation.rating_rationale: Anti-anchoring is decisive here: MMR 827 and the 13.2%/yr 'appreciation' both derive from just 6 transactions across a 17-unit block — meaningless and not to be trusted. With only 17 units, exit liquidity is near-nil; a single motivated seller sets the market and price discovery is poor. Developer (Mushroom Realty) has built only this one project — no track record. Gross yield is a weak 2.6%. The 999-year tenure and 990m to the future Serangoon North CRL station (~2030) are real positives that prevent an Avoid, and $1.58M is an accessible entry. But for a 5-7yr investment hold, the illiquidity and unreliable data dominate — Neutral, low confidence. Not a 'buy on the score'.
